Income-statement items are CUMULATIVE from 1 January 2026 (column header '01 January 2026 to 30 June 2026'), flagged via the _cumulative suffix — same convention as CITYBANK and as EBL's own 2026_Q1.json. Unusually, this particular filing ALSO discloses a discrete second-quarter-only column ('01 April 2026 to 30 June 2026') as a bonus, which is not part of line_items but was used for cross-validation (see below). EXTRACTION NOTE: same font-encoding corruption as 2026_Q1.json affects this filing's Solo section under plain pdftotext -layout (e.g. the Solo balance sheet heading literally mis-renders as 'As at 30 June 2025' — confirmed via OCR to actually read 'As at 30 June 2026'; the year is correct, this was purely a digit-glyph rendering bug, not a real error in the source document). All figures below were sourced via OCR (pdftoppm 300dpi + tesseract) of the Solo Balance Sheet/P&L/notes pages (PDF pages 7-9, 16). Cross-validated: (1) internal arithmetic — operating_income - operating_expenses = operating_profit exactly (16,470,154,536 - 7,067,111,028 = 9,403,043,508); operating_profit - total_provision = PBT exactly (9,403,043,508 - 1,659,760,061 = 7,743,283,447); PBT - tax = PAT within BDT 1 of rounding (7,743,283,447 - 3,452,296,746 = 4,290,986,701 vs reported 4,290,986,700); assets = liabilities + equity within BDT 1 of rounding; classified_loans/gross_loans = 15,195,976,748/466,056,410,455 = 3.261%, matching the filing's own reported NPL% of 3.26%. (2) the comparative '31 December 2025' column matches bank_financials/EBL/quarterly/2025_Q4.json exactly for every line item checked (same set as 2026_Q1.json). (3) discrete Q2-only PAT (2,288,522,963, from this filing's bonus column) plus 2026_Q1.json's profit_after_tax_cumulative (2,002,463,737) = 4,290,986,700, matching this filing's own H1 cumulative PAT exactly — strong cross-check that both quarters were read correctly. NOTABLE PATTERN (see also insights.json): total_equity dips from Q1's 53,053m to Q2's 51,149m despite Q2 alone being solidly profitable (PAT 2,289m). This is fully explained, not a data error: paid-up capital rose 15,958m to 16,437m (bonus share issue) and dividend equalisation reserve rose 356m to 1,154m, both funded out of retained earnings, alongside an implied cash dividend outflow — consistent with an AGM approving and paying the FY2025 dividend during Q2 2026 (Apr-Jun), a seasonal pattern not previously visible in this dataset's Q4-only series.

insights.methodology: Every insight cites the specific ratio/period pair it is derived from in ratios_timeseries.json.

risk_signals.statement: Unlike Dhaka Bank, Dutch-Bangla Bank, AB Bank, and Al-Arafah Islami Bank in this dataset, EBL shows no FY2024 stress dip: NPL ratio kept falling from FY2020's 2.72% through most of the period, ROE rose every year from FY2021 (15.51%) to FY2025 (19.13%), and CAR stayed in a tight, healthy 14-15.5% band. FY2025's NPL ratio (2.24%) is the lowest in the full 15-year series.

CAR was noticeably thinner in the early part of the series, bottoming at 10.18% in FY2011 (barely above the regulatory minimum) before climbing steadily to a consistent 12-15.5% range from FY2015 onward — the opposite trajectory from banks in this dataset that weakened over time.
ROE has stayed above 10% in every one of the 15 years, with a high of 19.13% in FY2025 and a low of 10.93% in FY2014 — one of the more consistently profitable banks researched in this dataset.
Total assets grew from BDT 117.6bn (FY2011) to BDT 761.6bn (FY2025), a 6.5x increase (13.9% CAGR), with the fastest acceleration from FY2021 onward (BDT 388.8bn to BDT 761.6bn in 4 years).

insights.historical_context: EBL stands out in this dataset as one of the few banks with no FY2024 sector-stress signal — NPL ratio and ROE both improved through FY2024 and FY2025 while several peers (Dhaka Bank, Dutch-Bangla Bank, AB Bank, Al-Arafah Islami Bank) show a clear NPL spike and profitability dip in FY2024. Combined with a CAR that has stayed comfortably above the regulatory minimum for a decade, this points to EBL being a comparatively resilient credit through the recent Bangladesh banking-sector stress period covered by this dataset.
insights.data_gaps: Q4/year-end (audited) data is available for all 15 years 2011-2025. Q1/Q2(Half-Yearly)/Q3 unaudited interim data has now been backfilled for 2017-2026 (30 quarters; 2026 partial through Q2, Q3 2026 not yet due as of the 2026-08-26 retrieval date) — see quarterly/<year>_Q1.json etc. 2011-2016 interim reports were located on ebl.com.bd (~18 more quarters, PDFs downloaded and verified but not yet parsed into this dataset) and remain a genuine gap pending a future session; this is a time-boxing gap, not a source-availability gap. Total liabilities was not directly reported in the annual report's source tables for any year and is calculated as total assets minus shareholders' equity throughout (both Q4 and the new interim quarters), so the balance-sheet-identity check for this bank is definitionally exact rather than an independent cross-check.

intra_year_patterns.statement: EBL's paid-up capital jumps between the Q1 and Q2 (Half-Yearly) interim filings in 8 of the 10 years checked (2017, 2019, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026) — a bonus share issue and cash dividend payment for the prior fiscal year, approved at the AGM, consistently lands in Q2 (Apr-Jun). Paid-up capital is flat Q1-to-Q2 in exactly two years, 2018 and 2020; the 2020 gap coincides with Bangladesh's COVID-19 lockdown period, a plausible AGM-delay explanation. This also explains a recurring artifact: a bank's EPS for a given Q1/H1 is often shown as a smaller '(restated)' figure in later reports' comparative columns than the value the contemporaneous report itself stated, purely from the enlarged post-bonus share count under IAS 33 — the underlying PAT is unchanged (confirmed identical in every instance checked, e.g. 2025_Q1.json's contemporaneous EPS 1.33 vs 2026_Q1.json's comparative-column EPS 1.13 for the same quarter, same PAT 1,805,234,242 both times).

The loan-to-deposit ratio (calculated) has fallen sharply and steadily from a 96-98% band throughout 2022-2023 to 76.6% by 2026_Q2 — deposits have grown considerably faster than the loan book over the last two years (e.g. total_deposits +24.0% YoY vs gross_loans +3.9% YoY at 2026_Q2), a distinct funding/balance-sheet-mix shift not visible in the Q4-only series, which only shows LDR settling in the high-80s/mid-90s by FY2024-2025 without revealing how much further it continued falling intra-2026.

sources.notes: annual_reports/EBL archive covers all 15 years 2011-2025 with no gaps. Complete Q4/year-end coverage for all 15 years achieved from just three annual reports' embedded multi-year highlights tables: the 2015 report's 'Five-Year Progression of EBL' (2011-2015), the 2020 report's 'Five-Year Progression'/'Horizontal Analysis' (2016-2020), and the 2025 report's 'Five-year Progression of Financials' (2021-2025). These are unusually detailed tables (balance sheet, income statement, capital, asset quality, efficiency ratios all in one place), giving this bank one of the most complete datasets researched so far. Q1/Q2(Half-Yearly)/Q3 unaudited interim data has now been backfilled for 2017-2026 (30 quarters, all Solo/Standalone basis, sourced directly from ebl.com.bd's /quarterly-reports and /financial-reports archives) — see the 'unaudited_quarterly_financial_statements' entries below for the full per-year source list. 2011-2016 interim PDFs were located and confirmed live on the site (~18 more quarters) but were not parsed this pass; this is a time-boxing gap only, not a source-availability gap — see the 'not_yet_parsed' entry below for the exact URLs to resume from. The 2026-vintage filings (Q1 and Half-Yearly) use a different, fuller 24-page 'Condensed Consolidated and Separate Financial Statements' template than 2011-2025's compact 2-page press-release format, and this new template's Solo-section font has a pdftotext extraction bug (digit glyphs mis-map, e.g. '1'<->'L', '5'<->'s', '0'<->'O') — those two files' figures were sourced via OCR (pdftoppm 300dpi + tesseract) of the same PDF pages instead, cross-validated three independent ways (see 2026_Q1.json/2026_Q2.json period_note for full detail). A genuine one-time restatement was found affecting FY2023 year-end figures specifically: every 2024-vintage interim filing's 31-Dec-2023 comparative column shows total_equity=BDT 39,767m and fixed_assets=BDT 8,517m, vs this dataset's existing 2023_Q4.json (sourced from the FY2025 annual report's five-year table) showing total_equity=BDT 37,484m and fixed_assets=BDT 5,994m — see 2024_Q1.json's period_note for the full reconciliation (total_liabilities matches exactly, isolating the gap to equity/fixed-asset classification). A separate, much smaller (~0.12% of total assets) comparative gap was found for FY2017 only, isolated similarly. Neither existing Q4 file was edited to 'fix' either discrepancy, per project rule. A recurring seasonal pattern was also found: EBL's paid-up capital jumps between Q1 and Q2 in 8 of the 10 years checked (bonus share issue + AGM dividend, consistently landing in Q2/Apr-Jun), with only 2018 and 2020 as gap years (2020 plausibly COVID-related) — see insights.json.
